deities: Goddess Rajarajeswari (main deity, form of Durga/Parvati)
Lord Shiva (lingam under the banyan tree within the premises)
festivals: Navaratri (September-October; nine-day festival, last two days Vijayadashami and Mahanavami celebrated with a grand elephant procession of nine decorated elephants)
Mullakkal Chirappu (November-December; 41-day festival, the town's biggest celebration, with elephant processions, fireworks, cultural programmes and annadanam)
Thaipooyakavadi (November-December; about fifteen kavadis take part in the procession)

history.dynasty: Traditionally attributed to King Devanarayana (Devanarayanan Thampuran) of Chembagasery; administered today by the Travancore Devaswom Board
history.period: Nearly 500 years old; current Rajarajeswari idol consecrated 16 July 1962
history.summary: The Mullakkal Rajeshwari Temple, in the heart of Alappuzha town, is nearly 500 years old and dedicated to Goddess Rajarajeswari, believed to be the mother of Alappuzha. Its name comes from the jasmine garden ('mullakkal' - jasmine place) in which the idol was first placed. Origin legends converge on King Devanarayana of Chembagasery: one story says exiled soldiers from Thekkumkur brought the idol and enshrined it in a jasmine garden where the king later built the temple; another says the king, enchanted by the goddess at Kodungallur Bhagavathy temple, dreamt she would follow him home, and when he rested in Alappuzha with his umbrella in the garden, the umbrella could not be moved - a sign the goddess wished to remain; a third says Namboodiri Brahmins fleeing Tipu Sultan's invasion brought an Annapurneswari idol and enshrined it there. Until 1961 the inner sanctum held Annapurneswari (with ladle and pot), standing and facing west. In 1961 a stranger entered the sanctum and embraced the idol, after which cracks appeared; the priests took it as the goddess's command to make a new idol, and on 16 July 1962 a 4-feet tall Rajarajeswari idol was consecrated in its place. Later the idols of Krishna and the serpent deities were added in separate shrines. The temple is built in traditional Kerala style with a distinctive open roof over the main shrine.

name: Mullakkal Rajeshwari Temple
town_description: Alappuzha (Alleppey), on the Arabian Sea coast in central Kerala, is known as the 'Venice of the East' for its backwaters, houseboats, lagoons and canals. It is a major port and trade town historically linked with coir, coconut and spice commerce, and today a leading backwater-tourism destination with the annual Nehru Trophy Boat Race on Punnamada Lake.

travel.airport: Cochin International Airport at Nedumbassery (approx. 70-90 km; taxis and app cabs available).
travel.railway: Alappuzha Railway Station (approx. 4-5 km), well connected to Kochi, Thiruvananthapuram and Chennai; autos and private buses run to the temple via Mullakkal town.
travel.road: In the heart of Alappuzha town at Mullakkal (Mullackal Road, 688011). Alappuzha lies on NH-47 (old numbering) and is connected by road to all main towns of South India; the temple is easily reached by auto-rickshaw, bus or taxi from anywhere in town.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather. Navaratri (September-October) and the 41-day Mullakkal Chirappu (November-December) are the most vibrant times to visit, with elephant processions and cultural programmes.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Morning 4:30 AM to 10:30 AM; evening 5:00 PM to 8:00 PM, open all days (verify - one official district tourism page lists 5:00 AM to 12:00 noon and 5:00 PM to 9:00 PM). No entry fee; traditional dress preferred (dhothi for men, saree for women); footwear not allowed inside.
